title: Validator reads stale baked default schemas instead of the declared namespace registry
description:
Default-origin rule assertions derive from the declared registry at validation time; the on-disk default schemas become write-through projections that can no longer desync validation.

## Background

Observed in this repository: `[namespaces.enforces]` has been declared in `.jit/config.toml` since the invariants epic, yet the first `enforces:` label ever applied failed the `namespace-registry` rule. The baked schema `.jit/schemas/default-namespace-registry.json` still carried a namespace pattern without `enforces`; the validator reads that file as authority, so a legitimate hand edit of the declared registry silently invalidated validation, and the failure surfaced at label-use time, far from the causal config edit. Manual schema repair was the workaround.

The mechanism gap: default schemas are baked from the registry at scaffold time, and no non-test code path regenerates them afterward (`ruleset_store` carries a regeneration helper with no production caller). The declared registry in `config.toml` is the source of truth; the baked schema is a copy treated as authority — the machine-artifact analogue of the staleness defect named by @/inv/single-source-prose.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Validation builds default-origin rule assertions (`label-format`, `namespace-registry`, `type-hierarchy-known`, the `namespace-unique-*` family) from the declared config registry in memory at load; on-disk schema files are not read as the authority for these rules.
- [hard] REQ-02: `schemas/default-*.json` files remain as projections for external consumers and are refreshed from the registry whenever jit writes `config.toml` or `rules.toml`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Custom rules (`origin` other than `default`) keep reading their declared schema files exactly as today.
- [hard] REQ-04: Regression test: in a fixture repo, hand-declare a new namespace in `config.toml`, apply a label in it, and `jit validate` passes with no intervening regeneration step.
- [hard] REQ-05: After the fix lands, this repository's `schemas/default-*.json` match the declared registry (projections refreshed by the landing change).

## Notes

Decisions pinned during intake:

- **Derive at load.** Rejected: regenerate-on-write only — a hand edit of `config.toml` stays stale until some jit write happens; and drift-check plus a `jit rules sync` command — the failure still occurs and adds a manual step, when the registry alone can answer the question the schema was baked to answer.
- **Priority high.** The breakage surfaces at label-use time, disconnected from the causal edit, so the misdiagnosis cost dominates the one-line workaround.
